title: Field-extension detection of lines on a variety with algebraically closed constants
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a smooth geometrically integral affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For every tower of field extensions $k\subseteq K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension], put $X_K=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $X_L=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $q:X_L\to X_K$ be the projection. For every invertible module $N$ on $X_K$ [def-sc-invertible-module], if $q^*N\cong\mathcal O_{X_L}$, then $N\cong\mathcal O_{X_K}$, where pullback is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Equivalently, scalar extension is injective on the groups of isomorphism classes of invertible modules, with tensor product as group law. The ground field $k$ is algebraically closed; neither $K$ nor $L$ is required to be algebraic over $k$.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, printed pp.12-13: perfect-closure reduction and the paragraph asserting clopenness via normal projective compactifications and Picard theory; supporting the historical alteration/Picard route beneath det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3). Agent-extracted geometric-triviality detection input. Related normal-compactification method: Guralnick--Jaffe--Raskind--Wiegand, On the Picard group: torsion and the kernel induced by a faithfully flat map, proof of Theorem 5.2, Step 1, pp.21-22 (arXiv:alg-geom/9410031); that theorem itself has extra resolution and algebraicity hypotheses and is NOT being cited as an exact statement of this node.

proof.text: Choose $j:X\hookrightarrow C$ and boundary primes $B_1,\ldots,B_r$ by [lem-sfb-algclosed-affine-normal-projective-boundary]. For $F=K,L$, write $U_F=j_F(X_F)\subset C_F$. Both $C_K,C_L$ are normal integral Noetherian projective schemes, hence proper. Their boundary prime divisors are exactly $B_{i,K},B_{i,L}$, and all these primes are geometrically integral over the respective fields. Since $(C_K)_E=C_E$ and $((B_i)_K)_E=(B_i)_E$ for every extension $E/K$, $C_K$ is geometrically integral and geometrically normal over $K$ and the $B_{i,K}$ are geometrically integral prime divisors over $K$, as the scalar comparison used in steps 2 and 3 requires.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-normal-divisorial-open-restriction], extend $N$ on $U_K$ to a coherent reflexive rank-one module $F$ on $C_K$. By [lem-sfb-geonormal-divisorial-scalar-comparison], its scalar pullback $F_L$ is coherent reflexive of rank one. Its restriction to $U_L$ is $q^*N$, which is trivial by hypothesis. Apply the boundary-kernel clause of the dictionary on $C_L$: there are integers $n_i$ such that $F_L\cong\mathcal O_{C_L}(\sum_i n_i B_{i,L})$. This is a boundary-divisor expression over $L$, not a claim that the original trivialization descends.

proof.text: Put $D_K=\sum_i n_i B_{i,K}$ and $H=(F\otimes\mathcal O_{C_K}(-D_K))^{**}$. The dictionary gives a coherent reflexive rank-one $H$ with $H|_{U_K}\cong N$, since $D_K$ is supported in the boundary. Scalar comparison and the reflexive tensor law give $H_L\cong(\mathcal O_{C_L}(D_L)\otimes\mathcal O_{C_L}(-D_L))^{**}\cong\mathcal O_{C_L}$, where $D_L=\sum_i n_iB_{i,L}$. The coefficients $n_i$ need not descend as a chosen divisor of a section: the same integer list defines $D_K$ because each boundary prime is defined over $k$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] in degree zero to the proper $K$-scheme $C_K$, the flat extension $K\to L$ (flatness of the map of base spectra is [lem-pc-field-extension-flat]) and the quasi-coherent $H$. Together with $H_L\cong\mathcal O_{C_L}$ (step 3) and [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety](2) on the geometrically integral proper $L$-scheme $C_L$, this gives an $L$-linear isomorphism $\Gamma(C_K,H)\otimes_K L\cong\Gamma(C_L,H_L)\cong L$. Thus $\Gamma(C_K,H)$ has dimension one over $K$: extension of a $K$-basis is an $L$-basis of the tensor product. Choose a nonzero $s\in\Gamma(C_K,H)$ and an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset C_K$ with $s|_V\neq0$ in $M=\Gamma(V,H)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $V_L=V\times_KL=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_KL)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] for the projection $V_L\to V$ the map $M\otimes_A(A\otimes_KL)=M\otimes_KL\to\Gamma(V_L,H_L)$, $m\otimes1\mapsto m_L$, is an isomorphism. Since $K\to L$ is a $K$-linear injection with a $K$-linear retraction, $M\to M\otimes_KL$ is injective, so $s_L|_{V_L}=(s|_V)_L\neq0$ and the scalar pullback $s_L\in\Gamma(C_L,H_L)$ is nonzero. Under an isomorphism $H_L\cong\mathcal O_{C_L}$, $s_L$ becomes a nonzero element of $\Gamma(C_L,\mathcal O_{C_L})=L$, hence a global unit; consequently the pulled-back section morphism $\mathcal O_{C_L}\xrightarrow{s_L}H_L$ is an isomorphism. No canonicity of the abstract base-change isomorphism is used.

proof.text: The section morphism $\mathcal O_{C_K}\xrightarrow{s}H$ is an isomorphism. Indeed on any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset C_K$, put $M=\Gamma(V,H)$. Pullback to $V_L=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_K L)$ is the tensor extension of $A\xrightarrow{s|_V}M$, by the affine-spectrum fibre-product identification and the natural affine-sections pullback isomorphism. The map $A\to A\otimes_K L$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]. Exactness of flat tensor [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies the tensored kernel and cokernel with the kernel and cokernel after extension. They vanish since $s_L$ is an isomorphism. Faithfully flat detection [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero] makes both original modules zero. Thus $A\to M$ is bijective on every affine open, so the affine tilde/global-sections equivalence makes $s$ an isomorphism on every affine open, hence an isomorphism of sheaves.

proof.text: Restrict $H\cong\mathcal O_{C_K}$ to $U_K$ and use $H|_{U_K}\cong N$ to obtain $N\cong\mathcal O_{X_K}$. For injectivity on isomorphism classes, if $N_1,N_2$ have isomorphic pullbacks, apply the proved assertion to $N_1\otimes N_2^\vee$ and tensor the resulting trivialization with $N_2$. Conversely injectivity implies the stated triviality test by taking $N_2=\mathcal O_{X_K}$.
